There is something about a quiet start, before messages and meetings pile up, that makes deep or creative work come more easily. By mid-afternoon my attention tends to be more fragmented, so I save routine or collaborative tasks for then.

That said, it depends on the work: mornings for anything that needs real focus, afternoons for lighter, social, or administrative stuff. If I had to pick just one, morning wins.
